title: AWS Serverless Part 1: Serverless Architecture on AWS
content: 8 min readMay 27, 2024--Press enter or click to view image in full sizeTraditional Server-based architectureIn traditional server-based architecture, applications are deployed on servers which must be provisioned, maintained, and scaled by the developer or the operations team.Press enter or click to view image in full sizePress enter or click to view image in full sizeThe provisioning, management, and patching of servers are time-intensive tasks that typically requires dedicated operations staff. Setting up and operating a non-trivial environment effectively is challenging. While infrastructure and hardware are essential elements of any IT system, they can also divert attention from the core focus — solving the business problem.What is a serverless architecture?A serverless architecture is a way to build and run applications and services without having to manage infrastructure.Compares the deployment and operational tasks in a traditional to those in a serverlessWhy Is AWS a Great Platform for Serverless?Function as a service from AWS Lambda, Microsoft Azure Functions, Google Cloud Functions, and IBM OpenWhiskServerless architectures are the latest advance for developers and organizations to think about, study, and adopt. This exciting new shift in architecture will grow quickly as software developers embrace compute services such as AWS Lambda.The AWS serverless platform includes a number of fully managed services that are tightly integrated with AWS Lambda and well-suited for serverless applications. Developer tools, including the AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM), help simplify deployment of your Lambda functions and serverless applications.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeWorking closely with customers and monitoring industry trends has allowed AWS to quickly iterate ideas and launch several important serverless services in areas such as APIs, functions, data stores, data streaming, AI, machine learning, event transportation, workflow and orchestration, and more.Idea of Running Everything as a ServicePress enter or click to view image in full sizeInfrastructure as a service (IaaS) represents the bare bones of a cloud platform — the network, compute, and storage resources, commonly housed in a data center. A high-level understanding of IaaS is beneficial as it forms the basis for serverless.Platform as a service (PaaS) is a service abstraction layer on top of IaaS to offer an application development environment in the cloud. It provides the platform and tools needed to develop, run, and manage applications without provisioning the infrastructure, hardware, and necessary software, thereby reducing complexity and increasing development velocity.Software as a Service (SaaS) is probably the most used and covers many of the applications we use daily, for tasks such as checking email, sharing and storing photos, streaming movies, and connecting with friends and family via conferencing services.Press enter or click to view image in full sizePress enter or click to view image in full sizeDatabase as a service (DBaaS) is a type of SaaS that covers various data storage options and operations. Along with the traditional SQL relational database management systems (RDBMSs), several other types of data stores are now available as managed services, including NoSQL, object storage, time series, graph, and search databases.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeFunction as a service (FaaS)In simple terms, FaaS is a type of cloud computing service that lets you run your function code without having to provision any hardware yourself. FaaS provided a core piece of the cloud computing puzzle by bringing in the much-needed compute as a service, and it soon became the catalyst for the widespread adoption of serverless.Principles of serverless architectures1 . Use a compute service to execute code on demand (no servers).Serverless architectures build upon the concepts service-oriented architecture (SOA). In a serverless setup, all custom code is developed and executed as isolated, independent, and often fine-grained functions within a stateless compute service like AWS Lambda.Developers can write functions to execute almost any common task, from reading and writing to a data source, to making calls to other functions, and executing calculations. For more complex scenarios, developers can construct complex pipelines and coordinate the execution of multiple functions. While there may be scenarios where a server is necessary, these situations are kinda rare, and developers are generally advised to minimize direct server management and interaction whenever possible.2 . Write single-purpose stateless functions.Code written for a compute service such as Lambda should be created in a stateless style. It must not assume that local resources or processes will survive beyond the immediate session. Statelessness is powerful because it allows the platform to quickly scale to handle an ever-changing number of incoming events or requests.As a software engineer, it’s beneficial to design functions follow the single responsibility principle (SRP). Functions dedicated to a singular task are easier to test, more robust, fewer bugs and unexpected side effects. By orchestrating a composition of such functions and services, you can maintain complex back-end systems that remain understandable and manageable. Moreover, granular functions with clearly defined interfaces are also more likely to be reused within a serverless architecture.For Lambda, code should be written in a stateless manner. It must not assume that local resources or processes will survive beyond the immediate session. The power of statelessness is to enable the platform to scale quickly in response to ever-changing number of incoming events or requests.3 . Design push-based, event-driven pipelines.Serverless architectures can be designed for any purpose. Systems may be developed from the ground up as serverless, or existing monolithic applications can be re-engineered to leverage this architecture. The most flexible and powerful serverless designs are those that are event-driven.Building event-driven, push-based systems often leads to reduced costs and complexity, as there’s no need to run additional code to check for changes, and can enhance the overall user experience. While event-driven, push-based models are an excellent aim, they may not always be suitable or appropriate in every situation. At times, it might be necessary to implement a Lambda function that polls for events or operates on a fixed schedule.Press enter or click to view image in full sizeSQS queue between API Gateway and Lambda — asynchronous connection between the API request and Lambda4 . Create thicker, more powerful front ends.It’s important to ensure that custom code executed in Lambda is fast. Functions that complete quickly cost less, as Lambda’s pricing depends on the number of requests, execution duration, and allocated memory. Moreover, a well-designed front end that communicates directly with third-party services can enhance the user experience.However, not all tasks are suitable for the front end, especially those involving sensitive information that cannot be exposed to the client device. Tasks like processing credit card transactions or sending emails to subscribers should be handled by a backend service, out of reach from the end user.In such instances, a compute service is necessary to coordinate actions, validate data, and maintain security. Consistency is another critical factor; if the front end is tasked with writing to multiple services and encounters a failure, it can leave the system in an inconsistent state. In this scenario, a Lambda function should be used because it can be designed to gracefully handle errors and retry failed operations.5 . Embrace third-party services.Third-party services are encouraged to participate if they add value and minimize the need for custom code. However, it is understood that when considering a third-party service, one must evaluate factors such as price, capability, availability, documentation, and support must be assessed.. Developers find it more beneficial to dedicate time to addressing problems unique to their field rather than duplicating features that others have already developed.Don’t reinvent the wheel, just realign it.Anthony J. D’AngeloConsidering ServerlessServerless is not a silver bullet in all circumstances. It may not be appropriate for latency-sensitive applications or software with specific service-level agreements (SLA).Not for everyone Lambda operates in a public cloud, and thus, it may not be ideal for mission-critical applications such as banking, life-support systems,… . Organizations might consider using dedicated hardware or establishing private or hybrid clouds with their own compute services to fulfill serviceability and reliability criteria.Vendor lock-in is another issue. When developers decides to use third-party APIs and services, such as AWS, they risk creating an architecture that is heavily dependent on the chosen platform. It is crucial to carefully evaluate the consequences of vendor lock-in and the dangers of utilizing third-party services, which encompass aspects like company stability, data sovereignty, privacy, expenses, support, documentation, and the range of features offered.Decentralization Moving from a monolithic approach to a more decentralized serverless approach doesn’t automatically reduce the complexity of the underlying system either. It introduces its own challenges because of the need to make remote rather than in-process calls and the need to handle failures and latency across a network.When to use serverlessServerless architecture allows developers to focus on software design and code rather than infrastructure. Scalability and high availability are easier to achieve, and the pricing is often fairer because you pay only for what you use. Importantly with serverless, you have a potential to reduce some of the complexity of the system by minimizing the number of layers and amount of code you need.NO MORE SERVERSLOW COSTLESS CODESCALABLE AND FLEXIBLEServerless applications will be cheaper to run and faster to implement. There’s also a need to reduce complexity and costs associated with running infrastructure and carrying out development of traditional software systems. The reduction in cost and time spent on infrastructure maintenance and the benefits of scalability are good reasons for organizations and developers to consider serverless architectures.Reference:Serverless Architectures on AWS — Peter SbarskiServerless Development on AWS — Sheen Brisals & Luke HedgeServerless Land.
